work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
ref: Matthew 1:1-6 (verse divisions as printed in WH)
original: Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυεὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ. Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ, Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζαρὰ ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐσρώμ, Ἐσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀρὰμ, Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών, Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βοὲς ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βοὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί, Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυεὶδ τὸν βασιλέα.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops)
english: own translation (G5): The book of the genesis of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham. Abraham begat Isaac, Isaac begat Jacob, Jacob begat Judah and his brothers, Judah begat Perez and Zerah by Tamar, ... Jesse begat David the king.
translator: own translation (G5), not a published translation
page: page unknown (printed page not visible in the scan; PDF page 13 shows the running head KATA MAQQAION and the signature B 2)
what_it_says: Matthew's title calls Jesus son of David and son of Abraham before any mention of Joseph, and the list then runs through Judah's line (Tamar), Rahab, Ruth, and David.
limits: Shows only WH's printed text, not the apparatus. Accents were read from crops of a 300-dpi render; the djvu OCR of the same page is noisy and was not used for the reading.

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυεὶδ τὸν βασιλέα. Δαυεὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου, Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ, Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζείαν, Ὀζείας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops)
english: own translation (G5): Jesse begat David the king. David begat Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife, Solomon begat Rehoboam, Rehoboam begat Abijah, Abijah begat Asaph, Asaph begat Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat begat Joram, Joram begat Uzziah, Uzziah begat Jotham.
what_it_says: Matthew's list goes from Joram directly to Uzziah (Ozias), with no Ahaziah, Joash or Amaziah in between, and names Asaph where 1 Chr 3:10 has Asa.
limits: The Greek shows the skip but not the reason. Whether Asaph here is a textual error for Asa is a variant question; the WH apparatus was not read, so no variant claim is made. Verse 8 and 9 numbering is standard, not checked in WH's margin.

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσείαν, Ἰωσείας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος. Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβάβελ, Ζοροβάβελ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops)
english: own translation (G5): Manasseh begat Amon, Amon begat Josiah, Josiah begat Jechoniah and his brothers at the deportation to Babylon. After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begat Salathiel, Salathiel begat Zerubbabel, Zerubbabel begat Abiud.
what_it_says: Josiah is said to beget Jechoniah directly, which skips Jehoiakim; Jechoniah then begets Salathiel after the Babylonian exile.
limits: Jehoiakim is not named; 1 Chr 3:15-16 names him as Josiah's second son and Jeconiah's father (see item G5-13). Shows the printed text only.

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μαθθάν, Μαθθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος Χριστός.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops)
english: own translation (G5): Eliud begat Eleazar, Eleazar begat Matthan, Matthan begat Jacob, Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus who is called Christ.
what_it_says: Matthew's line ends with Joseph as husband of Mary, and the relative pronoun 'of whom' (ex hes, feminine) is the only point where Mary is named as the source of Jesus's birth.
limits: The feminine relative shows the birth is from Mary; it does not state Mary's own descent from David, which is a separate question. Some opponents read the feminine as making Mary a genealogical link; the verse itself does not say so.

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυεὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυεὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops)
english: own translation (G5): So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.
what_it_says: Matthew states three sets of fourteen generations, with the Babylonian exile as the middle boundary.
limits: Own count from the WH text of 1:2-16: 41 names after Abraham (Isaac to David = 14; Solomon to Jechoniah = 14; Salathiel to Jesus = 13). The 14 in the third set is reached only by a counting convention; the convention itself is UNVERIFIED here and was not checked against a commentator.

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: Τοῦ δὲ [Ἰησοῦ] Χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν. Μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσὴφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου. Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν. Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος Κυρίου κατ᾽ ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυείδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops). Square brackets around Ἰησοῦ are printed by WH as printed in the scan (WH's sign for doubtful text; the Introduction was not read to confirm the category)
english: own translation (G5): Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child of the Holy Spirit. Joseph her husband, being righteous and not wanting to expose her, resolved to put her away quietly. While he considered these things, behold an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, Joseph son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife.
what_it_says: The angel addresses Joseph as 'son of David' and tells him to take Mary as his wife, which is the text on which the Joseph-is-Davidic argument rests.
limits: The vocative 'Joseph son of David' gives Joseph's Davidic status, not Mary's. The verse does not say that Mary is of David's house; that is an inference (see Chrysostom item G5-09).

work: The New Testament in the Original Greek (text of Westcott and Hort)
author: Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
original: τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. ... καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως [οὗ] ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1 (text), Cambridge: Macmillan, 1881 (archive.org scan newtestamentinor1881west, PDF pages 13-15 read as page images; accents read from 300-dpi crops). Square brackets around οὗ in 1:25 as printed (WH's doubtful-text sign)
english: own translation (G5): She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. ... and he did not know her until she bore a son; and he called his name Jesus.
what_it_says: Joseph is told to name the child (2nd person 'you shall call'), and the next verse says he did so, which is Matthew's basis for treating the naming as Joseph's act.
limits: The text shows Joseph naming the child; it does not state a legal adoption or legal paternity. That reading needs an argument from Jewish law, which is not in the verse. The brackets on οὗ are WH's own doubt sign.

work: The Four Gospels in Syriac from the Sinaitic Palimpsest (Lewis 1894), English translation
author: Agnes Smith Lewis (translator); Syriac from the Sinaitic palimpsest
date: palimpsest c. 4th-5th century AD; edition 1894 AD
ref: Matthew 1:16 (verse as numbered in the translation)
original_edition: Syriac original NOT extracted: the archive.org djvu OCR of fourgospelsinsyr0000unse (https://archive.org/details/fourgospelsinsyr0000unse) is garbled and the Syriac phrase for Mt 1:16 could not be located; not rendered from the page image
english: Jacob begat Joseph; Joseph, to whom was betrothed Mary the Virgin, begat Jesus, who is called the Christ.
translator: Agnes Smith Lewis (1894 translation, as OCR'd from archive.org copy translationoffou00lewi)
page: page unknown (OCR text, printed page not determined)
edition: A translation of the four Gospels from the Syriac of the Sinaitic palimpsest, 1894 (publisher not read; check title page)
what_it_says: In the Sinaitic Syriac as translated by Lewis, Mt 1:16 reads 'Joseph ... begat Jesus' with Joseph named as the one betrothed to Mary, not 'Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom'.
limits: English translation only; the Syriac was not read, so the claim that the Syriac has 'begat' cannot be checked here. Lewis's translation may render a Syriac participle or relative differently. Not a Lk=Mary witness; it is a textual form of Mt 1:16. Cureton marks in the translation are not analysed.

work: I Chronicles 3:10-12
author: Chronicler (Hebrew Bible)
original: וּבֶן־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה רְחַבְעָ֑ם אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנֽוֹ׃ יוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֛וֹ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנֽוֹ׃ אֲמַצְיָ֧הוּ בְנ֛וֹ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ יוֹתָ֥ם בְּנֽוֹ׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: The son of Solomon: Rehoboam; his son Abijah, his son Asa, his son Jehoshaphat, his son Joram, his son Ahaziah, his son Joash, his son Amaziah, his son Azariah, his son Jotham,
what_it_says: The Chronicler lists Joram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah (Uzziah) and Jotham as successive sons, so Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah are present here and absent from Matthew 1:8.
limits: Shows the omission by comparison only; Matthew's own reason for the omission is not in Chronicles. The Chronicles list itself is a royal genealogy, not a claim about Mary.

work: II Kings 8:24-26
author: Deuteronomistic history (Hebrew Bible)
original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹרָם֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ {פ} בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן־אַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹרָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃ בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בְמׇלְכ֔וֹ וְשָׁנָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְשֵׁ֤ם אִמּוֹ֙ עֲתַלְיָ֔הוּ בַּת־עׇמְרִ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: Joram rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David; his son Ahaziah succeeded him as king. In the twelfth year of King Joram son of Ahab of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king of Judah. Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year; his mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of King Omri of Israel.
what_it_says: Ahaziah son of Joram is recorded as king of Judah after Joram, aged twenty-two, reigning one year; this is the first of the three kings Matthew omits.
limits: The text confirms the reign of Ahaziah, which Matthew does not list; it does not say why he was skipped.

work: II Kings 14:1-3
author: Deuteronomistic history (Hebrew Bible)
original: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן־יוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־יוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃ בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמׇלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֙שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ (יהועדין) [יְהוֹעַדָּ֖ן] מִן־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֛ה יוֹאָ֥שׁ אָבִ֖יו עָשָֽׂה׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: In the second year of King Joash son of Joahaz of Israel, Amaziah son of King Joash of Judah became king. He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother’s name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem. He did what was pleasing to GOD, but not like his forefather David; he did just as his father Joash had done.
what_it_says: Amaziah son of Joash becomes king of Judah in the second year of Joash of Israel, which is the third omitted king in Matthew 1:8.
limits: Confirms that Amaziah existed as Joash's son; not a reason for the omission.

work: I Chronicles 3:15-19
author: Chronicler (Hebrew Bible)
original: וּבְנֵי֙ יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֔הוּ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יֽוֹחָנָ֔ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖י יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים הַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ הָרְבִיעִ֖י שַׁלּֽוּם׃ וּבְנֵ֖י יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים יְכׇנְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃ וּבְנֵי֙ יְכׇנְיָ֣ה אַסִּ֔ר שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֖ל בְּנֽוֹ׃ וּמַלְכִירָ֥ם וּפְדָיָ֖ה וְשֶׁנְאַצַּ֑ר יְקַמְיָ֥ה הוֹשָׁמָ֖ע וּנְדַבְיָֽה׃ וּבְנֵ֣י פְדָיָ֔ה זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל וְשִׁמְעִ֑י וּבֶן־זְרֻבָּבֶל֙ מְשֻׁלָּ֣ם וַחֲנַנְיָ֔ה וּשְׁלֹמִ֖ית אֲחוֹתָֽם׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: The sons of Josiah: Johanan the first-born, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum. The descendants of Jehoiakim: his son Jeconiah, his son Zedekiah; and the sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son, Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah; the sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei; the son[s] of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith was their sister;
what_it_says: Josiah's sons include Jehoiakim (second son), Jehoiakim's son is Jeconiah, and Jeconiah's son is Shealtiel, who is Zerubbabel's father; this is the Chronicler's line that Matthew 1:11-12 condenses.
limits: Chronicles has Jehoiakim as the one omitted in Matthew 1:11 and makes Shealtiel 'son of Jeconiah'; Luke 3:27 gives Shealtiel as son of Neri, a conflict noted in the page's general brief but not analysed here.

work: Jeremiah 22:30
author: Jeremiah (Hebrew Bible)
ref: Jeremiah 22:30 (Hebrew verse 30 = 7th element of the Sefaria array)
original: כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה כִּתְב֞וּ אֶת־הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ עֲרִירִ֔י גֶּ֖בֶר לֹא־יִצְלַ֣ח בְּיָמָ֑יו כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יִצְלַ֜ח מִזַּרְע֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וּמֹשֵׁ֥ל ע֖וֹד בִּיהוּדָֽה׃ {פ}
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: Thus said  GOD:Record this man as without succession,One who shall never be found acceptable;For none of his offspring shall be acceptedTo sit on the throne of DavidAnd to rule again in Judah.
what_it_says: The verse says that Coniah (Jeconiah) is to be recorded as childless, that none of his seed shall sit on David's throne or rule again in Judah (JPS English).
limits: The Hebrew 'mizarco' (of his seed) is the core of the objection. Matthew's line passes through Jeconiah's son Shealtiel (1 Chr 3:17), so the objection is that Joseph cannot be a king's heir. The answers in the page's brief (Joseph as legal father; Solomon/Nathan lines) are not drawn here. Sefaria's English has a doubled phrase at 22:24 (an artifact); 22:30 is clean.

work: Jeremiah 36:30
author: Jeremiah (Hebrew Bible)
original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה עַל־יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד וְנִבְלָתוֹ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה מֻשְׁלֶ֔כֶת לַחֹ֥רֶב בַּיּ֖וֹם וְלַקֶּ֥רַח בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: Assuredly, thus said GOD concerning King Jehoiakim of Judah: He shall not have any of his line sitting on the throne of David; and his own corpse shall be left exposed to the heat by day and the cold by night.
what_it_says: Jehoiakim is told that none of his line will sit on David's throne, which is the verse usually cited for why Jehoiakim might be left out of a royal line.
limits: The verse concerns Jehoiakim; it does not say that Matthew omitted him for this reason. The link is a hypothesis, not a claim the text makes.

work: Genesis 46:12
author: Pentateuch (Hebrew Bible)
original: וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה עֵ֧ר וְאוֹנָ֛ן וְשֵׁלָ֖ה וָפֶ֣רֶץ וָזָ֑רַח וַיָּ֨מׇת עֵ֤ר וְאוֹנָן֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ חֶצְרֹ֥ן וְחָמֽוּל׃
original_edition: Hebrew: Masoretic text as hosted on Sefaria ('Miqra according to the Masorah'), read from Sefaria API JSON; English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition as hosted on Sefaria
english: Judah’s sons: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah—but Er and Onan had died in the land of Canaan; and Perez’s sons were Hezron and Hamul.
what_it_says: Perez's sons, Hezron and Hamul, are listed as the sons of Perez, whereas Hezron is Judah's grandson.
limits: This is NOT a skipped-generation case: it names Perez's sons directly. It was checked as a possible example of 'begat' for grandsons and it does not supply one. Genesis 46:18 and 46:25 (Zilpah and Bilhah 'these she bore to Jacob') were fetched but are also not skip examples. The OT skip evidence that does apply is 1 Chr 3:11-12 against Mt 1:8 (item G5-10), and Ezra 7:1-5 against 1 Chr 6, which was NOT fetched.

work: Homilies on the Gospel of Saint Matthew, Homily II (on Matt 1:1)
author: John Chrysostom
ref: Homily II on Matthew 1:1 (Matt I.1), NPNF1 vol. 10; exact section number not confirmed
original_edition: Greek not read: PG 57 scans tried (archive.org patrologiaecurs57migngoog: Greek but no Matthew homilies found; bim 1860 vol 57: Latin, no Greek Matthew) did not yield Hom. II
english: 'he hath traced the genealogy of her espoused husband, and shown him to be of the house of David. For when this hath been clearly proved, that other fact is demonstrated with it, namely, that the Virgin likewise is sprung from thence, by reason that this righteous man ... would not have endured to take a wife from another race.'
translator: NPNF1 vol. 10 (translator named on the title page of NPNF1-10 was not read)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, First Series, vol. 10 (New York: Christian Literature Co., 1888)
what_it_says: Chrysostom says Matthew traced Joseph's genealogy to David and that this shows the Virgin is also of David's house, because the righteous Joseph would not marry outside the family.
limits: Chrysostom states Mary's Davidic descent as a consequence of Joseph's marriage rule; he does not mention Luke or Heli, and he does not say Luke gives Mary's line. Greek original not located.

work: De consensu evangelistarum (Harmony of the Gospels), Book II, ch. III 5-6
author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: De consensu evangelistarum II.3.5-6 (NPNF1 section numbering 5-6; Latin Cons. 2.3.5-6)
original_edition: Latin not read: a 1857 Migne PL 34-labelled scan on archive.org (patrologiaecurs34migngoog) does not contain the Harmony text
english: Luke ... 'Joseph who was the son of Heli' ... Joseph may have had two fathers, namely one by whom he was begotten, and a second by whom he may have been adopted. For it was an ancient custom also among that people to adopt children ... (section 5). And section 6: even although Luke had said that Joseph was begotten by Heli, that expression ought not to disturb us ... there is nothing absurd in saying that a person has begotten, not after the flesh, it may be, but in love, one whom he has adopted as a son.
translator: Rev. William Findlay (credited in the NPNF1-06 header; check title page)
page: NPNF1-06 (printed page not determined; bracketed numbers [671]-[676] in that edition are not read as Migne columns here)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, First Series, vol. 6 (New York: Christian Literature Co., 1887), ed. Philip Schaff
what_it_says: Augustine answers the Harmony objection by proposing that Joseph had two fathers, one by nature and one by adoption, and that the evangelists name different ones.
limits: Augustine's solution is adoption, not Mary's line. The editor's note in NPNF1-06 (footnote 673) says that 'many scholars' hold that Luke gives Mary's lineage as Heli's daughter; that note is by the editor, NOT by Augustine, and must not be quoted as Augustine. The same footnote reports Augustine's Retractations correction (see G5-17).

work: Retractationes II.16 (as reported in the NPNF1-06 editor's footnote 673)
author: Augustine of Hippo
original_edition: Latin not read. Only the English footnote and its quoted Latin fragments ('alteri' / 'ab altero adoptatus') were read, in NPNF1-06 footnote 673; the primary Retractationes text was not found online in the searches run
english: (from editor's footnote) In his Retractations (ii. 16) Augustin alludes to this passage with the view of correcting his statement regarding the adoption. He tells us that he should not have said that there 'was one by whom Joseph was begotten, and another by whom he may have been adopted,' but should rather have put it thus: 'one by whom he was begotten, and another unto whom he was adopted' (alteri instead of ab altero adoptatus). And the reason indicated for the correction is the probability that the father who begat Joseph was the mother's second husband, who, according to the Levirate law, had married her on the death of his brother without issue.
translator: editor's paraphrase in NPNF1-06 footnote (not Augustine's words)
what_it_says: Per the editor, Augustine later says he should have worded the father-by-adoption clause differently, and gives a levirate reason for the father who begat Joseph.
limits: Secondhand. The footnote's levirate reading is the editor's report of Augustine's correction; the exact Latin of the retraction must be checked before the page quotes it. The footnote's words 'Augustin passes over this solution' are the editor's comment.

work: Ecclesiastical History I.7, quoting Africanus, Epistle to Aristides
author: Julius Africanus (quoted by Eusebius of Caesarea)
date: Africanus c. 220-240 AD (epistle, approx.); Eusebius c. 325 AD
ref: Eusebius, Historia ecclesiastica I.7.1-8 (Africanus, Ep. ad Aristidem, as quoted)
original_edition: Greek not read (GCS Eusebius not located in this run); English read in NPNF2-01 sections 1-8
english: For Joseph was the son of Eli, the son of Melchi. ... For Matthan and Melchi at different periods had each a son by one and the same wife ... Thus shall we find Jacob and Heli, though of a different race, yet by the same mother, to have been brethren. ... (sections 1-8 read; §5: 'if, with Luke, we reckon them from Nathan the son of David, in like manner the third from the end is Melchi, whose son Eli was the father of Joseph.')
translator: Arthur Cushman McGiffert (NPNF2 vol. 1 translator per ccel header)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 1 (ed. Schaff; Eusebius, Church History) — Eusebius text
what_it_says: Africanus (as quoted by Eusebius) says Matthan and Melchi shared one wife, so Jacob and Heli were half-brothers; Eli is Joseph's legal father, while Jacob is his natural father. Mary's father is not named in the sections read.
limits: In the sections read (1-8) Africanus does not say Eli is Mary's father; the Lk=Mary reading is not in this text. Africanus is the earliest surviving levirate solution in this set; the Greek wording was not checked.
source_url: https://ccel.org/ccel/s/schaff/npnf201/cache/npnf201.txt (NPNF2-01 full text; page-level URL not checked)

work: Catena Aurea on Matthew 1:16 (Jerome, Commentary on Matthew, quoted by Aquinas)
author: Thomas Aquinas (compiler), quoting Jerome
ref: Catena Aurea, Matthew ch. 1 verse 16, gloss 'Jerome' (Jerome's Commentary on Matthew, book 1)
original_edition: Latin of Jerome not read: Migne PL 26 scans tried (patrologiaecurs26migngoog) are PG 135 (chronicle tables), not PL 26; Jerome's commentary text was not located. The English below is Aquinas's quotation of Jerome
english: Jerome: This passage is objected to us by the Emperor Julian in his Discrepancy of the Evangelists. Matthew calls Joseph the son of Jacob, Luke makes him the son of Heli. He did not know the Scripture manner, one was his father by nature, the other by law.
translator: William Whiston (Catena Aurea English, London: Rivington, 1842, per ccel header; check title page)
page: not determined (Catena ccel text; Matthew ch. 1 section read)
edition: Catena Aurea, English trans. (1842, Whiston per ccel header)
what_it_says: Jerome answers Julian's objection by saying Joseph had one father by nature (Jacob) and one by law (Heli), and cites levirate law and Africanus / Eusebius for the mechanism.
limits: Quotation of Jerome through a medieval compilation, in a 19th-century translation, not Jerome's own text. Does not say Heli is Mary's father. Jerome's Lk=Mary status must be checked in his Latin (not done here).
source_url: https://ccel.org/ccel/a/aquinas/catena1/cache/catena1.txt (Catena Aurea full text; Matthew ch. 1 gloss)
